inputs.share_count_basis: 4,046.9m equity shares outstanding at 31-Mar-2026 (FY2026 20-F statement of changes in equity, line 10304, post the 100m-share Nov/Dec-2025 tender buyback) plus ~7.3m dilutive options/RSUs (FY2026 diluted minus basic weighted count, 4,120.1m vs 4,112.8m) = ~4,054m fully diluted. 1 ADS = 1 equity share. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows; buybacks are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat.
inputs.cash_note: Cash and cash equivalents 2,287 + current investments 837 + non-current investments 924 at 30-Jun-2026 (Q1 FY2027 IFRS USD press release balance sheet). Investments are almost entirely liquid treasury (CDs, commercial paper, quoted debt, liquid mutual funds) with ~$100m of strategic unquoted equity. The $600m fall from 31-Mar-2026 (4,648) reflects the June final dividend and a Q1 acquisition (goodwill +$466m). Their income is excluded from the forward flows (EBITDA is operating-only), so the assets go in the bridge -- the matching-asset rule.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest on financial assets 305 (note 2.16: 184 amortised cost + 121 FVOCI) less the 127 'interest and dividend income' the cash-flow statement already reverses out of OCF (received in investing) = ~178 left inside reported OCF. Stripped because ~$4.0bn of cash and investments is added in the bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 20-F consolidated cash flow statement, 'Stock compensation expense' 108 (95 FY2025, 79 FY2024). India-style net-share settlement taxes are not separately disclosed and are immaterial; no combined adjusted-EBITDA figure published.
inputs.lease_payments_note: FY2026 payment of lease liabilities 318 (financing) + lease finance cost ~41 (finance cost accrued 41 of 47 total) = 359, 1.78% of revenue. Charged inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path (treatment B).
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.5% on USD flows: US 10y ~4.3% + beta ~1.0 x 5.0% ERP = ~9.3%, plus ~0.25pp for an India-domiciled, INR-cost-base issuer; no debt so WACC = cost of equity. Same WACC in every scenario -- AI-disruption and H-1B risk are charged in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not in the rate (adaptations f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: full lease cash payment (principal 318 + interest ~41 = 359, 1.78% of revenue) deducted via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (967 at Mar-26) EXCLUDED from net debt; da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (552 - 213 ROU = 339, 1.68% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is ~0.1% of profit (net profit 3,316 vs attributable 3,313). Flows are consolidated; the NCI stock of 55 (30-Jun-2026) is deducted once in the equity bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, with the non-US adaptations (USD-reporting Indian filer with INR cost base, IFRS-16 leases, tiny NCI, large treasury book). Routed per dcf-methods SKILL.md: a mature, debt-free, asset-light IT-services operating company -- not a financial, REIT or holdco. First valuation of INFY (no MEMORY.md entry). Statements are IFRS consolidated in USD (presentation currency; INR functional at parent); ADR quotes in USD, 1 ADS = 1 share, so no FX conversion. EBITDA margin path is PRE-SBC (operating profit 4,085 + D&A 552 + SBC 108 = 4,745, 23.5% of FY2026 revenue; 24.2% ex the one-off $143m India Labour Codes charge). Q1 FY2027 operating margin 21.1% and FY2027 guidance of 20-22% map to ~24.0-24.5% on this definition. Owner FCF = reported 3,733 - SBC 108 - interest income in OCF 178 = 3,447; the forward build additionally charges lease payments (359) which reported FCF leaves in financing, so the like-for-like FY2026 owner FCF after leases is ~3,088, against a modelled base year-1 of ~3,050. Working capital is NEGATIVE capture (-15% of the revenue increase): receivables + unbilled grow with revenue (FY2026 net WC outflow 259 on +881 revenue; FY2025 70 on +715). Buybacks: a genuine repurchaser -- $2,006m tender in FY2026 under the policy of returning ~85% of 5-year cumulative FCF; the flat count is funded. SBC is small (0.54% of revenue) but nonzero, so the house/street band is narrow, not collapsed. PRICE: the 52-week high of 30.0 printed on the week of 2025-12-15 is a bad tick (weekly close 20.22, surrounding weeks 17-19); the real 52-week range is ~10.3-20.2. The stock has de-rated ~35% since January 2026 on the GenAI-disruption thesis for offshore IT services.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-1.3% 5yr, 2.2% 3yr) is meaningless as a growth proxy: Infosys returns ~85% of FCF via dividends and buybacks (FY2026: $2.1bn dividends + $2.0bn buyback against $3.3bn profit), so book value does not compound. It diverges >30% from revenue and EPS CAGRs. Revenue 3yr CAGR selected as the growth anchor; the 5yr revenue CAGR (8.2%) is inflated by the FY2022 post-COVID digital boom (+20%) and is not a forward guide.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series = reported FCF - SBC (interest-in-OCF not reconstructed pre-FY2024; it is ~$0.1-0.2bn and roughly flat, so CAGRs are barely affected). The 3yr owner-FCF CAGR (13.6%) starts from FY2023's working-capital trough (FCF 2,534 vs 3,055 in FY2022) and overstates the trend; the 5yr 4.4% is the better read. SBC is growing faster than revenue (45 -> 108 over five years, 0.33% -> 0.54% of revenue) but remains immaterial, so the SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs differ by only ~0.2-0.3pp.

base.growth_rates_note: FY2027 2.5% (guidance 1.5-3.0% cc, Q1 +2.4% cc / +2.9% USD); large-deal TCV ($14.9bn FY26, 55-61% net new) and AI services (8.2% of revenue) lift growth to ~4% mid-decade, below the 8% 5yr history because GenAI deflates legacy app-maintenance billing.
base.ebitda_margin_path_note: Pre-SBC EBITDA. 24.2% = midpoint of 20-22% operating-margin guidance + D&A 2.7% + SBC 0.55%; drifts down 0.4pp as clients claw back AI productivity gains in pricing.
base.cash_tax_rate_path_note: FY2026 ETR 26.4%, FY2024 cash 25.6%; FY2025's 662 cash tax was refund-assisted and is not a base.

scenario_narratives.base: Infosys stays a low-single-digit grower: FY2027 lands at the top half of the lowered 1.5-3.0% guidance, then large-deal bookings and AI services (Topaz, 8.2% of revenue and growing double digits sequentially) roughly offset GenAI deflation in application maintenance and testing, holding USD growth near 3.5-4% through FY2031 before fading to 3%. Project Maximus keeps operating margin inside the 20-22% band, but clients capture part of the AI productivity gain, so pre-SBC EBITDA eases from 24.2% to 23.8%. Cash conversion stays near 100% of net profit and the ~85% payout policy keeps returning it.
scenario_narratives.bull: Infosys repositions as the AI-implementation partner rather than a labour-arbitrage vendor: record large-deal TCV with a rising net-new mix converts to revenue, AI services scale from 8% toward a quarter of revenue at better pricing, and the industry consolidates spend onto fewer, larger partners. USD growth recovers to 6-7% by FY2029 (well below the FY2022 boom but above the FY2024-27 trough), the H-1B fee stays vacated, and operating leverage plus a mix shift toward platforms (Finacle, Topaz) lift pre-SBC EBITDA to 25%.
scenario_narratives.bear: GenAI is structural, not cyclical: 25-30% of traditional app-development, testing and maintenance work is automated away and passed through to clients, producing the 10-12% revenue headwind over 3-4 years that AI-services revenue only partly offsets. Revenue falls ~6% cumulatively FY2028-FY2030 before stabilising at 1-1.5% growth; pricing pressure from TCS, Accenture and Cognizant, H-1B costs (fee reinstated on appeal, DOJ penalty) and a US/Europe IT-budget freeze compress pre-SBC EBITDA to 21% (operating margin ~18%). Still debt-free and cash generative -- the bear is a shrinking annuity, not a solvency story.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: GenAI disruption of the offshore labour model is a credible structural threat the company has not yet disproven, guidance has already been cut once this year, and H-1B/DOJ outcomes are binary. Base 50% because bookings and margins have so far held up. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right (AI revenue scaling, pricing holding, a demand recovery and benign visa policy).

valuation_philosophy.summary: A debt-free, cash-generative IT-services franchise valued on owner FCF after SBC and full lease cost, with ~$4.0bn of liquid treasury added at book. The question the price is asking is not near-term earnings (FY2027 guidance is intact on margin) but terminal durability under GenAI: the bear case is a shrinking annuity, the bull an AI-implementation re-rating. Risk is charged in the bear flows and a 25% bear weight, not stacked into the discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: GenAI automation of application maintenance/testing deflating billable revenue faster than AI services grow
Pricing pressure as clients demand AI productivity gains be passed through
US H-1B fee reinstatement on appeal and the DOJ visa-classification investigation
US/Europe enterprise IT-budget cyclicality (~88% of revenue)
INR/USD moves: rupee appreciation compresses USD margins (costs mostly INR)
Terminal value is 43-57% of EV (Gordon binds in all three scenarios, just under the caps; implied exit 11.9x/14.6x/15.8x owner FCF)
